title: The Two Ways
aka: the way of life and the way of death
lead: From Moses to Jesus, the Bible pictures life as a choice between two paths: one leading to life and blessing, the other to death. Jewish and early Christian teachers built whole lessons on this picture.

sections.b: Moses sets before Israel "life and good, death and evil" and urges them to choose life (Deuteronomy 30:15–19). Psalm 1 contrasts the way of the righteous, which the LORD watches over, with the way of the wicked, which will perish. Proverbs keeps returning to the path of wisdom and the path of folly (Proverbs 4:18–19), and Jeremiah 21:8 offers "the way of life and the way of death." Jesus speaks of the narrow gate and the wide road (Matthew 7:13–14).

The Epistle of 1 Enoch (1 Enoch 91–105) is built on "the paths of righteousness" and "the paths of violence." The Dead Sea Scrolls teach two spirits, of truth and of deceit (Community Rule 3–4). The early Christian Didache begins: "There are two ways, one of life and one of death," and the Epistle of Barnabas 18–20 has a similar section.
